name: stochastic_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when the index sells off sharply enough within a 70-second window to push the stochastic below 20, it reflects that aggressive order flow has briefly overwhelmed the available bid-side liquidity at that depth. The moment %K crosses above %D from the oversold zone, it marks the first measurable slowdown in the rate of decline — resting limit buy orders and institutional delta hedges begin absorbing the selling pressure. This creates a micro-reversion of 10-20 NIFTY spot points over the subsequent 30-90 seconds, captured by entering ATM calls on the cross bar. The inverse holds symmetrically for overbought crosses: supply absorbs demand at the short-term range top and the index fades 10-20 spot pts.

indicators.name: stoch_k_14
indicators.purpose: 14 bars at 5s = 70-second range position, smoothed with 3-bar SMA. NOT 12x the original (which would be 168 bars = 14 min). We are trading the FAST reversion from a 70-second extreme, not a 14-minute one. At our 15-90 second hold, the trigger window must be shorter than the hold time — 70s detects the exhaustion of the immediate selling pressure while 14-min detects multi-hour regime shifts that are not actionable at 5s.

indicators.name: stoch_d_14_3
indicators.purpose: 3-period SMA of %K adds 15 seconds of lag. The cross (%K above %D) is the entry trigger: it confirms that the immediate rate of decline has reversed, not just that price hit an extreme. Same smoothing as original because the signal logic (cross confirmation) is unchanged — only the timescale is compressed.

indicators.name: vwap_session
indicators.formula: Cumulative TPVOL / Cumulative VOL from 09:15 IST each day
indicators.purpose: No scaling needed — VWAP is cumulative from session open. Used as a proximity filter: only trade when NIFTY is within 0.5% of VWAP. Ensures we are trading micro-reversions around fair value, not chasing moves that are part of a larger directional trend away from VWAP.

conditions: stoch_k < oversold_threshold (default 20) — NIFTY near bottom of 70-second range
stoch_d < oversold_threshold — smoothed %K also in oversold zone (no false cross)
stoch_k[t] > stoch_d[t] AND stoch_k[t-1] <= stoch_d[t-1] — bullish cross just occurred
close > vwap * (1 - vwap_proximity) — within 0.5% below VWAP (near fair value)
close > open — bullish bar at the cross (confirming buying pressure on this bar)
bars_consecutive_in_oversold < 30 — oversold for < 2.5 min (not trending down)
buy_ce.confirmation: Bullish close bar on the stochastic cross bar itself

conditions: stoch_k > overbought_threshold (default 80) — NIFTY near top of 70-second range
stoch_d > overbought_threshold — smoothed %K also in overbought zone
stoch_k[t] < stoch_d[t] AND stoch_k[t-1] >= stoch_d[t-1] — bearish cross just occurred
close < vwap * (1 + vwap_proximity) — within 0.5% above VWAP (near fair value)
close < open — bearish bar at the cross
bars_consecutive_in_overbought < 30 — overbought for < 2.5 min (not trending up)
buy_pe.confirmation: Bearish close bar on the stochastic cross bar itself

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. A 70-second range overshoot on NIFTY reverts within 30-90s when the thesis holds; if the index moves more than 8 spot pts against the position (continuing past the range extreme), the selling/buying is structural not exhausted and the thesis is invalid. Calibrated to NIFTY's 30-second typical move of 2-5 option pts — stop is just above the 1-sigma adverse move.
exit.target_rationale: 6 option points = ~12 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. A successful stochastic reversion from a 70-second extreme typically bounces 15-25 spot points as the stochastic reverts toward the midline (50). Targeting 12 spot pts captures approximately 50-60% of the typical bounce while maintaining 1:1.5 risk-reward. Consistent with NIFTY's 1-minute move range of 3-7 option pts.

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25 — above 25, NIFTY exhibits trending/gapping behavior where stochastic extremes persist rather than reverting
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST — skip first 15 minutes of noise; avoid EOD illiquidity
filters.volume_filter: none explicit — index volume is noisy at 5s; VWAP proximity serves as a more reliable filter
filters.trend_filter: bars_consecutive_in_extreme < 30 — if stochastic has been extreme for 2.5+ minutes, the index is trending and reversion trades will fail
filters.spread_filter: limit order execution at candle close — no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: high — stochastic crossovers are well-known TA signals; but at 5s on NIFTY the signal is far less crowded than at 1-min on equities because retail traders don't operate at this speed

adaptation_notes: Three key changes from original: (1) Lookback compressed from 14-min (14 × 1min) to 70-second (14 × 5s) because we are trading the fast intraday reversion, not the slow multi-minute one. (2) VWAP proximity threshold set to 0.5% instead of original 0.5% — same logic, same NIFTY levels since VWAP is an absolute price level. (3) Extended-extreme filter kept at 30 bars (2.5 min) vs original's 10 bars (10 min) — same ratio, catching the same 'trending stochastic' failure mode. The original was noted as unprofitable on stocks due to noise; on NIFTY index at 5s, the signal is cleaner because the index aggregates away single-stock noise, but the edge remains thin and filter discipline is critical.
weaknesses: Thin edge — stochastic cross is well-known and this exact setup fires infrequently (the VWAP + cross + bar confirmation stack is tight)
NIFTY trending sessions (RBI announcements, budget day) will generate repeated failed cross signals before the extreme resolves
At 5-second resolution, a single aggressive order in the futures market can create a 70-second 'false extreme' that immediately reverses the stochastic cross signal
